verses.text: King Solomon was king over all Israel.
These were the princes whom he had: Azariah the son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder;
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
Azariah the son of Nathan was over the officers; Zabud the son of Nathan was chief minister, the king’s friend;
Ahishar was over the household; and Adoniram the son of Abda was over the men subject to forced labor.
Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who provided food for the king and his household. Each man had to make provision for a month in the year.
These are their names: Ben Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
Ben Deker, in Makaz, in Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan;
Ben Hesed, in Arubboth (Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to him);
Ben Abinadab, in all the height of Dor (he had Taphath, Solomon’s daughter, as wife);
Baana the son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth Shean which is beside Zarethan, beneath Jezreel, from Beth Shean to Abel Meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;

Ben Geber, in Ramoth Gilead (the towns of Jair the son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead, belonged to him; and the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars, belonged to him);
Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali (he also took Basemath the daughter of Solomon as wife);
Baana the son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei the son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and he was the only officer who was in the land.
Judah and Israel were numerous as the sand which is by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and making merry.
Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
Solomon’s provision for one day was thirty cors  of fine flour, sixty measures of meal,
ten head of fat cattle, twenty head of cattle out of the pastures, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, and gazelles, and roebucks, and fattened fowl.
For he had dominion over all on this side the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings on this side the River: and he had peace on all sides around him.
Judah and Israel lived safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
Those officers provided food for king Solomon, and for all who came to king Solomon’s table, every man in his month. They let nothing be lacking.
They also brought Barley and straw for the horses and swift steeds to the place where the officers were, each man according to his duty.
God gave Solomon abundant wisdom and understanding, and very great understanding, even as the sand that is on the seashore.
Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.
For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all the nations all around.
He spoke three thousand proverbs; and his songs numbered one thousand five.
He spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that grows out of the wall; he also spoke of animals, of birds, of creeping things, and of fish.
People of all nations came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, sent by all kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.

footnotes.content: Watch how quickly the text moves from David's struggle to Solomon's settled reign. "King Solomon was king over all Israel"—no doubt, no rival, the kingdom at rest. The Lord gives what He promises.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Azariah the priest holds the highest place here. Notice—the spiritual leader listed first, even in a king's cabinet. It tells us what Solomon honored.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Scribes and recorders—those who write things down, who preserve memory and record. A kingdom that values literacy and truth-keeping. Solomon understood that wisdom speaks, but writing makes it last.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benaiah leads the army; Zadok and Abiathar both serve as priests—a careful balance. The king delegates power but does not abandon the sacred. Even war and worship answer to the throne.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zabud is called "the king's friend"—not just a title, but a real one. In a court full of officials, there is someone Solomon confides in. Friendship in high places is rarer than rank.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adoniram oversees forced labor—the hard work that builds a kingdom. Even in Solomon's golden age, there is toil behind the beauty. Some burdens are carried so others may flourish.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twelve officers, each serving a month—the kingdom's needs divide the year fairly. Solomon learned from the tribes' old structure. Good order mirrors creation's rhythm and rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ben Hur oversees the hill country of Ephraim—a specific place, a name, a trust. These are not abstract administrators but real men tied to real land, answerable to it and to the king.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beth Shemesh and Elon Beth Hanan are real places where judges once met. Solomon's officers inherit the land of his ancestors' faith. The kingdom's roots run deep.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ben Hesed tends Socoh and the land of Hepher—a shepherd of soil and seed. An officer's duty stretches beyond the throne room; he feeds the land that feeds the kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ben Abinadab married Solomon's daughter Taphath. The king binds his officers to his house through family. Love and loyalty become one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baana oversees Taanach and Megiddo, ancient battlegrounds where Israel once fought for the land. Now an officer rules them in peace. The past wars make the present rest precious.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ben Geber holds Ramoth Gilead and Argob in Bashan—sixty walled cities. Cities with walls speak of order, safety, and care. Solomon's wealth shows in fortified places, not just gold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ahinadab serves in Mahanaim, a place of memory—where Jacob once wrestled with God, where Ishbosheth fled. Each officer stands in a place thick with story.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ahimaaz married Solomon's daughter Basemath—another bond of kin. The king builds his kingdom not just through law but through family. Love ties stronger than chains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baana the son of Hushai tends Asher and Bealoth—faithful men in their posts, each one known by name. A kingdom is not great because of its size but because its people are known.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehoshaphat rules Issachar—a tribe known for "understanding the times." Perhaps Solomon chose him because he needed wisdom in that post.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shimei the son of Ela tends Benjamin, the smallest tribe—the one David came from. Even the least gets a careful hand. Solomon does not forget home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Geber rules Gilead, the land of Sihon and Og. He alone oversees this region—a burden and an honor. Faithful men carry heavier loads.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Judah and Israel were numerous as the sand...eating and drinking and making merry." The people are full, safe, and happy. This is what the kingdom's order creates—room for joy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the River to the Philistines, from Egypt's border to the coast—Solomon's reach extends as far as God promised. The tribute flows in because the nations know his peace is real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thirty cors of fine flour, sixty measures of meal—the king's table is fed with abundance. Even the grain lists speak of the Lord's blessing. Generosity begins with enough.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ten fat cattle, twenty from the pastures, a hundred sheep, deer, gazelles, fowl—such variety, such care in the selecting. A king's table reflects not greed but stewardship of plenty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Tiphsah to Gaza, all kings answer to Solomon, and he has peace on every side. The absence of war is itself the treasure. A ruled kingdom is a rested kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Every man under his vine and under his fig tree"—the ancient picture of safety. From Dan to Beersheba, the whole land hears the same promise. When a kingdom is at peace, all can plant and harvest and keep what is theirs.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty thousand stalls of horses, twelve thousand horsemen—Solomon's military might is real, but it does not march. He has strength to keep the peace, not hunger to break it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "They let nothing be lacking." The officers ensure the table is always full, the guests always honored. Generosity flows from the top down. A king's faithfulness shapes his servants' care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the horses are fed with barley and straw in their proper place. No creature is forgotten, no corner of the kingdom left untended. A well-run house cares for all that serves it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "God gave Solomon abundant wisdom...even as the sand that is on the seashore." The Lord's gift is measured not by gold but by understanding. Wisdom is the true riches Solomon received.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Solomon's wisdom exceeds the children of the east and all Egypt. The world's wisest bow to hear him. But remember—wisdom's test is not how it sounds but how it builds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ethan, Heman, Calcol, Darda—named wise men of old—yet Solomon surpasses them all. His fame goes to all nations. But fame rests on sand unless built on the fear of God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three thousand proverbs, one thousand five songs—a life spent shaping wisdom into words. Solomon did not hoard what God gave him. He made it sing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "From the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop"—from the greatest tree to the smallest plant, from beasts to fish. A wise man sees God's hand in all creation, not just in mighty things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this verse: the nations still hunger for wisdom that lasts. So many voices claim to teach, yet a word spoken from the fear of the Lord still turns heads. In a world of endless noise, a gentle truth still travels.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
